title: Diabetes diagnostic criteria
text: Diabetes may be diagnosed if A1c >= 6.5% on two separate tests or fasting plasma glucose >= 126 mg/dL. Prediabetes includes A1c 5.7% to 6.4%.

title: Metformin and kidney function
text: Metformin is generally avoided when eGFR < 30. For eGFR 30-45, consider dose reduction and monitor renal function more frequently.

title: LDL and statin intensity
text: For adults with LDL >= 190 mg/dL, high-intensity statin therapy is recommended unless contraindicated.

title: Hypertension treatment threshold
text: For most adults, initiate pharmacologic therapy if BP is persistently >= 140/90 mmHg after lifestyle counseling. Consider lower thresholds in higher-risk patients.

title: CKD staging reminder
text: eGFR < 60 for >= 3 months is consistent with chronic kidney disease. Assess albuminuria to refine risk.

title: Diabetes and statin use
text: Adults age 40-75 with diabetes generally benefit from at least moderate-intensity statin therapy; consider high-intensity statin for additional risk factors.

title: Lifestyle recommendations in prediabetes
text: For prediabetes, recommend weight loss, dietary modification, and regular physical activity. Recheck A1c periodically to monitor progression.

title: Hypertriglyceridemia note
text: Severe hypertriglyceridemia may increase pancreatitis risk. Address secondary causes and consider therapy based on overall risk and levels.

title: A1c testing frequency
text: For stable glycemic control, measure A1c at least twice per year; quarterly if therapy changes or goals not met.

title: Metformin monitoring in CKD
text: When metformin is used with reduced eGFR, monitor renal function more frequently and reassess dosing.

title: BP measurement best practices
text: Confirm elevated BP with proper cuff size and repeat measurements across visits when feasible.

title: Statin contraindications reminder
text: Consider liver disease, drug interactions, and patient tolerance when prescribing statins.

title: Hypoglycemia risk note
text: Hypoglycemia risk is higher with insulin and sulfonylureas; counsel patients on recognition and management.
